title: Planar Gradient Diffusion System to Investigate Chemotaxis in a 3D Collagen Matrix
protocol: Obtain a silicone elastomer kit.
Obtain a live cell imaging chamber.
Obtain a 22 mm glass coverslip.
Obtain a machined aluminum metal cube with dimensions 10.07 mm x 3.95 mm x 5.99 mm.
Place the coverslip in the bottom holder of the live cell imaging chamber.
Assemble the rest of the live cell imaging chamber as directed by the vendor.
Using forceps, place the machined aluminum metal cube in the middle of the live cell imaging chamber housing on top of the coverslip.
Set aside the assembled chamber with the aluminum metal cube inside.
Mix silicone elastomer solutions according to manufacturer’s protocol to make 5 ml of elastomer.
Pour silicone elastomer solution into the live cell imaging chamber setup using a disposable lab spatula.
Ensure not to move the placed machined aluminum metal cube during pouring.
Place the system on the lab bench in a safe location overnight for curing.
The next morning, deconstruct the live cell imaging chamber as recommended by the manufacturer.
Pull out the mold using forceps.
Using forceps, carefully extract the machined aluminum metal cube from the mold.
Rinse the mold with deionized water at the sink.
Place the mold on a paper towel to dry.
Once dry, use a hobby utility knife to cut slits through the mold spaced 2.34 mm apart from each longitudinal end inside the silicone mold.
Ensure the mold stays in a safe and dry place until you are ready to construct the system for an experiment.
Measure out 150 μl of 3-aminopropyl-trimethoxysilane and pour into a 50 ml tube.
Add 30 ml of 100% ethanol to the 50 ml tube with a second disposable pipette, close the lid, and vortex for 2 minutes.
Pour the solution in a glass Petri dish and set aside.
Pour 15 ml of 100% ethyl alcohol in a second Petri dish and set aside.
Measure out 30 ml of deionized water and pour into a 50 ml tube.
Measure out 1,875 μl of glutaraldehyde and pour into the same 50 ml tube, close the lid, and vortex for 2 minutes.
Pour the mixture in a third Petri dish and set aside.
Rinse both sides of one 22 mm round glass coverslip with 100% ethanol using a disposable pipette.
Place the rinsed glass coverslip into the 3-aminopropyl-trimethoxysilane solution for 5 minutes.
Rinse the glass coverslip again with 100% ethanol and place it into the glutaraldehyde mixture for 30 minutes.
Remove the glass coverslip from the mixture after 30 minutes using forceps.
Rinse the glass coverslip with deionized water and place onto dry tissue to air-dry overnight at room temperature.
Add 500 µl of tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl and 100 µl of acetic acid in a 50 ml tube.
Vortex the mixture for 2 min.
Pour the solution into a glass Petri dish.
Take one glass coverslip and dip it into the prepared mixed solution for 2 min.
Rinse the coverslip with deionized water using a disposable pipette.
Place the rinsed coverslip onto dry tissue to air-dry overnight at room temperature.
Store dried hydrophobic coverslips in plastic Petri dishes until needed.
Repeat the process of dipping and drying coverslips as required.
Before use, rinse molds with 90% ethyl alcohol using a disposable pipette over a waste container.
Place the mold in a Petri dish filled with deionized water and allow it to sit overnight.
Dry the mold by placing it on a towel.
Cut hydrophilic coverslips into two rectangles slightly larger than 3.95 mm x 5.99 mm using a high-precision diamond-scribing tool.
Slide each cut rectangle coverslip into the slots of the silicone mold.
Apply vacuum grease along the bottom of the silicone mold using a disposable pipette.
Flip the mold back right-side up and press the bottom onto the circular hydrophilic glass coverslip to create a seal.
Pick up the assembled mold with disposable gloves and place it into a disposable Petri dish.
Place the Petri dish containing the mold into a bio-hood.
Turn on UV Bio-hood lamp for 1 hour to sterilize the mold before experimentation.
Mix cell media and chemoattractant in a 15 ml tube according to standard protocols.
Pipette 5 ml of specific cell media-chemoattractant concentration solution into another 15 ml tube and move it into a heated water bath.
Extract 5 ml of just cell media using a pipette into a second 15 ml tube and place in a heated water bath for microscopy experiments.
Pipette 30 µl of 10x phosphate buffered saline (PBS) into a micro centrifuge tube.
Add 6 µl of 1 N sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to the micro centrifuge tube containing PBS and vortex for 15 seconds.
Obtain collagen I rat tail solution from the fridge using standard laboratory techniques and protocols.
Pipette 168.3 µl of cold collagen into the same micro centrifuge tube containing PBS and NaOH.
Add 18 μl of yellow-green fluorescent carboxylate-modified microspheres to the micro centrifuge tube using a pipette.
Vortex the micro centrifuge tube for 30 seconds.
Add 77.7 μl of cell media-cell mixture (approximately 2 x 10^6 cells/ml) into the micro centrifuge tube.
Mix the contents with a pipette tip for 20 seconds.
Pipette 300 μl of collagen-cell mixture into the center well (#2) of the prepared mold assembly.
Place the mold onto a disposable Petri dish and move it to a standard incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2 for 20 minutes.
Remove the system from the incubator and place it back into the bio-hood.
Using forceps, remove both hydrophobic cover slips by clamping onto the top of each coverslip and pulling up and away from the mold.
Move the whole system to the desired microscopy setup.
Under the microscope, using a 100 μl single-channel pipette, add 100 μl of cell media into well #1.
Using another 100 μl single-channel pipette, add 100 μl of cell media with the desired chemoattractant concentration into well #3.
Immediately commence imaging after adding solutions to both wells.
Make 5 µM rhodamine in a 15 ml tube using standard calculations and protocols.
Image the 3D collagen matrices with a confocal system mounted on an inverted microscope using an argon laser (488 nm) to capture fluorescence.
Image every 2 or 3 seconds for up to 7 hours.
Import images into computational software for rescaling and normalizing by maximum intensity.
Convert images to a gray color-map of the image to select the edge.
Pick an axis along the center of the image, to the right of the center and to the left of the center.
Using the computational software code, plot normalized intensity, true intensity, and the difference between the two.
Input parameters necessary for fitting (concentration, time, and length).
Plot normalized concentration versus time.
Plot concentration profile across the x-axis with a polynomial fit to the data.
Calculate the coefficient of diffusion using the computational software code.
Record the specific time that the chemokine was added to the system during chemotaxis experiments.
Ensure to record confocal time-lapse recording of cell migration movement and note the specific time and location from edge where imaging occurred.

Plug the noted elapsed time, location, and coefficient of diffusion for the specific cell into the equation to find the normalized specific concentration at any point within the collagen for both diffusion and cell experiments.
Start imaging 3D collagen matrices with a confocal system mounted on an inverted microscope after adding the desired chemoattractant concentration into well #3.
Place the moving cell in the middle of the field of view once a moving cell is found.
Utilize a piezoelectric motor to image every 1 or 2 min.
